title.narrative: Danish Red Cross and the Diplomatic Super Year

description.narrative: During the 2025 “Diplomatic Super Year”, Denmark simultaneously held key international leadership roles through its seat on the UN Security Council, the EU Presidency and chairship of the Arctic Council.

title.narrative: Strengthening Livelihoods for women in Afghanistan

description.narrative: In Afghanistan, ARCS has continued to deliver humanitarian services and facilitated vocational training for 420 women, primarily from female-headed households in hard-to-reach areas across the Herat, Nangarhar, Kabul and Helmand provinces. The services weredelivered by female ARCS staff, and enhanced women’s capacity to earn a livelihood and improved their overall well-being.

title.narrative: Community centres improved psychosocial wellbeing in Bangladesh

description.narrative: In Bangladesh, BDRCS has played a significant role in driving psychosocial and social improvements at individual and community level through community based MHPSS activities.

title.narrative: Strengthened MHPSS and community resilience in Sudan

description.narrative: In Sudan, the SRCS has contributed to strengthening the mental health, psychosocial wellbeing and resilience of refugees, internally displaced persons (IDPs), and host communities. Observations ofchildren from all groups show that children who participated in structured activities with SRCS have regained a sense of normalcy, social connection, and hope for the future despite having lived through the traumatic experiences of war and displacement.

title.narrative: Strengthened protection for migrants in Mali

description.narrative: Through sustained humanitarian diplomacy and collaboration with actors such as IOM, the Mali Red Cross has contributed to enhanced protection of migrants in Mali.

title.narrative: Strenghtening the Health System in Somalia

description.narrative: With support from DRC, SRCS actively collaborated and advocated with national health authorities, leading to the development of national clinical guidelines and SOPs for diabetes and hypertension management, ensuring treatment of non-communicable diseases (NCD) e.g. cardiometabolic diseases is integrated into basic health services. The health authorities’ ownership of the SOPs is critical for the sustainability of NCD care and its broader adoption in an environment where NCDs have long been overshadowed by communicable diseases.

title.narrative: Early Action and Response to El Nino Floods

description.narrative: The El Niño phenomena have since October 2023 contributed to above-average rainfall inKenya, resulting in floods and severe damages nationwide. In spite of the authorities indicating that there would be limited risks, KRCS initiated critical preparedness activities supported by DRC reaching 10.700 people with life-saving information early warning and risk information and 4.500 people with early maturing seeds to strengthen their resilienceto harvest losses. After the onset of the disaster, the support enabled KRCS to set-up 137 evacuation centres across the country and support with a variety of emergency response

title.narrative: Tigray Humanitarian Response Phase III - Meeting survival and well-being needs of conflict-affected populations

description.narrative: The humanitarian situation in Tigray remains critical. The implementation of the PeaceAgreement signed in November 2022 remain sporadic and humanitarian needs are rising in response to continued displacement, widespread food insecurity and significant scale-down of UN aid in response to aid diversion. With support from Denmark, ERCS have been able to – as one of very few organizations – continue providing humanitarian assistance to people living in Tigray including cash assistance, ambulance and health services, and water.

title.narrative: Healthy Minds for Palestinian Children and Youth

description.narrative: The increase in violence and restrictions in oPt have had severe consequences for thepsychosocial wellbeing of Palestinian children and youth. PRCS’s structured psychosocialactivities have strengthened the mental health and wellbeing of Palestinian children and youth through promoting calm, hope, sense of safety, connectedness and self-efficacy which reduces isolation and negative behaviours and fosters positive interactions in families.
